Authenticating requests

This API is not authenticated.

Administration

Handles the dashboard views and related data for federal (national) and state-level users.

LGA Completeness Scores

requires authentication

Returns completeness scores for all LGAs in a given state.

Example request:
curl --request POST \
    "http://localhost/administrator/completeness" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json" \
    --data "{
    \"state\": \"Lagos\"
}"

const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost/administrator/completeness"
);

const headers = {
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json",
};

let body = {
    "state": "Lagos"
};

fetch(url, {
    method: "POST",
    headers,
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
}).then(response => response.json());

Example response (200):


[
    {
        "name": "Ikeja",
        "y": 85
    },
    {
        "name": "Surulere",
        "y": 78
    }
]
Received response:
Request failed with error:

If you're a maintainer of ths API, verify that your API is running and you've enabled CORS.
You can check the Dev Tools console for debugging information.

Administration - Contact

APIs for handling contact messages and feedback submissions.

This controller allows users to submit messages via a public contact form and allows admins to view submitted messages. Emails are sent to admins with the feedback details.

List all contact messages (admin view).

Example request:
curl --request GET \
    --get "http://localhost/admin/messages?page=1" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json"
const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost/admin/messages"
);

const params = {
    "page": "1",
};
Object.keys(params)
    .forEach(key => url.searchParams.append(key, params[key]));

const headers = {
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json",
};

fetch(url, {
    method: "GET",
    headers,
}).then(response => response.json());

Administration - DHIS2 Synchronization

APIs for synchronizing healthcare facility data with DHIS2 (District Health Information System). Handles creation, updates, and deletion of organization units in DHIS2, including assignment of ownership and level of care groups. All operations are logged for audit purposes.

Create Facility in DHIS2

requires authentication

Creates a new organization unit (facility) in DHIS2 with all associated metadata including ownership, level of care, and optional level of care options. Automatically handles facility closure date based on operational status. Sends email notification to DHIS2 team upon success. All operations are logged to dhis_log table for audit trail.

Example request:
curl --request POST \
    "http://localhost/admin/hfr-dhis-exchange/store" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json" \
    --data "{
    \"id\": 12345,
    \"facility_name\": \"General Hospital Abuja\",
    \"alt_facility_name\": \"Gen Hosp Abuja\",
    \"state_id\": 1,
    \"ward_id\": 50,
    \"operational_status_id\": 1,
    \"ownership_id\": 1,
    \"facility_level_id\": 3,
    \"facility_level_option_id\": 0,
    \"start_date\": \"2020-01-15\",
    \"close_date\": \"2024-12-31\",
    \"postal_address\": \"P.O. Box 123, Abuja\",
    \"longitude\": \"7.3986\",
    \"latitude\": \"9.0765\",
    \"email_address\": \"info@hospital.com\",
    \"website\": \"https:\\/\\/hospital.com\",
    \"phone_number\": \"+234-123-456-7890\"
}"

const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost/admin/hfr-dhis-exchange/store"
);

const headers = {
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json",
};

let body = {
    "id": 12345,
    "facility_name": "General Hospital Abuja",
    "alt_facility_name": "Gen Hosp Abuja",
    "state_id": 1,
    "ward_id": 50,
    "operational_status_id": 1,
    "ownership_id": 1,
    "facility_level_id": 3,
    "facility_level_option_id": 0,
    "start_date": "2020-01-15",
    "close_date": "2024-12-31",
    "postal_address": "P.O. Box 123, Abuja",
    "longitude": "7.3986",
    "latitude": "9.0765",
    "email_address": "info@hospital.com",
    "website": "https:\/\/hospital.com",
    "phone_number": "+234-123-456-7890"
};

fetch(url, {
    method: "POST",
    headers,
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
}).then(response => response.json());

"Created"

Request   

POST admin/hfr-dhis-exchange/store

Headers

Content-Type        

Example: application/json

Accept        

Example: application/json

Body Parameters

id   integer     

HFR facility ID (used as DHIS2 code). Example: 12345

facility_name   string     

Facility name. Example: General Hospital Abuja

alt_facility_name   string  optional    

Alternative/short facility name. Example: Gen Hosp Abuja

state_id   integer     

State ID for parent organization unit lookup. Example: 1

ward_id   integer     

Ward ID for parent organization unit assignment. Example: 50

operational_status_id   integer     

Operational status: 1 (Operational), 2-4 (Temporarily closed - auto-sets close date), 5+ (Permanently closed - uses provided close date). Example: 1

ownership_id   integer     

Ownership type ID for group assignment. Example: 1

facility_level_id   integer     

Facility level/care level ID for group assignment. Example: 3

facility_level_option_id   integer  optional    

Facility level option ID. Use 0 to skip. Example: 0

start_date   date  optional    

Facility opening date. Example: 2020-01-15

close_date   date  optional    

Facility closure date (required if operational_status_id > 4). Example: 2024-12-31

postal_address   string  optional    

Postal address. Example: P.O. Box 123, Abuja

longitude   string  optional    

Longitude coordinate. Example: 7.3986

latitude   string  optional    

Latitude coordinate. Example: 9.0765

email_address   string  optional    

Email address. Example: info@hospital.com

website   string  optional    

Website URL. Example: https://hospital.com

phone_number   string  optional    

Phone number. Example: +234-123-456-7890

Update Facility in DHIS2

requires authentication

Updates an existing organization unit (facility) in DHIS2. Supports updating basic facility information and reassigning organization unit groups (ownership, level of care, level options). Only updates groups that are specified in the request data. Sends email notification to DHIS2 team upon success. All operations are logged.

Example request:
curl --request POST \
    "http://localhost/admin/hfr-dhis-exchange/update" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json" \
    --data "{
    \"id\": 12345,
    \"data\": [
        \"architecto\"
    ]
}"

const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost/admin/hfr-dhis-exchange/update"
);

const headers = {
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json",
};

let body = {
    "id": 12345,
    "data": [
        "architecto"
    ]
};

fetch(url, {
    method: "POST",
    headers,
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
}).then(response => response.json());

Example response (200, Success):


"Updated"

Example response (500, DHIS2 API Error):


"Exception_Error"

Example response (500, Facility Not Found in DHIS2):


"Exception_Error"

Example response (500, Failed to Get DHIS2 UID):

Request   

POST admin/hfr-dhis-exchange/update

Headers

Content-Type        

Example: application/json

Accept        

Example: application/json

Body Parameters

id   integer     

HFR facility ID. Example: 12345

data   string[]     

Update data containing two keys:

  • updates: Object with facility fields to update (name, shortName, address, coordinates, etc.)
  • groups: Object with group assignments to update (ownership_id, facility_level_id, facility_level_option_id) or "empty" to skip
updates   object  optional    

Facility fields to update in DHIS2.

groups   object|string  optional    

Organization unit groups to reassign. Use "empty" to skip group updates. Example: architecto

facility_name   string  optional    

Facility name for email notification. Example: General Hospital Abuja

ward_id   integer  optional    

Ward ID for email notification. Example: 50

Delete/Close Facility in DHIS2

requires authentication

Attempts to delete a facility from DHIS2. If deletion fails due to associated data (DataValue), automatically closes the facility instead by setting the closure date. Handles three scenarios:

  1. Successful deletion (no data associated)
  2. Closure (has associated data, cannot be deleted)
  3. Failure (other errors)

Sends appropriate email notifications to DHIS2 team. All operations are logged.

Example request:
curl --request POST \
    "http://localhost/admin/hfr-dhis-exchange/delete" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json" \
    --data "{
    \"id\": 12345,
    \"facility_name\": \"General Hospital Abuja\",
    \"alt_facility_name\": \"Gen Hosp Abuja\",
    \"state_id\": 1,
    \"ward_id\": 50,
    \"start_date\": \"2020-01-15\",
    \"postal_address\": \"P.O. Box 123, Abuja\",
    \"longitude\": \"7.3986\",
    \"latitude\": \"9.0765\",
    \"email_address\": \"info@hospital.com\",
    \"website\": \"https:\\/\\/hospital.com\",
    \"phone_number\": \"+234-123-456-7890\"
}"

const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost/admin/hfr-dhis-exchange/delete"
);

const headers = {
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json",
};

let body = {
    "id": 12345,
    "facility_name": "General Hospital Abuja",
    "alt_facility_name": "Gen Hosp Abuja",
    "state_id": 1,
    "ward_id": 50,
    "start_date": "2020-01-15",
    "postal_address": "P.O. Box 123, Abuja",
    "longitude": "7.3986",
    "latitude": "9.0765",
    "email_address": "info@hospital.com",
    "website": "https:\/\/hospital.com",
    "phone_number": "+234-123-456-7890"
};

fetch(url, {
    method: "POST",
    headers,
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
}).then(response => response.json());

View DHIS2 Operation Logs

requires authentication

Displays a complete audit trail of all DHIS2 synchronization operations including creates, updates, deletes, and group assignments. Shows status of each operation and any error details for troubleshooting.

Example request:
curl --request GET \
    --get "http://localhost/admin/hfr-dhis-exchange/logs" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json"
const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost/admin/hfr-dhis-exchange/logs"
);

const headers = {
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json",
};

fetch(url, {
    method: "GET",
    headers,
}).then(response => response.json());

Retry Failed DHIS2 Operations

requires authentication

Attempts to retry previously failed DHIS2 operations (create, update, or group assignments). Retrieves facility data from database and reattempts the failed operation based on the log entry. Useful for handling temporary network issues or DHIS2 server downtime.

Example request:
curl --request POST \
    "http://localhost/admin/hfr-dhis-exchange/resend" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json" \
    --data "{
    \"log_id\": 456,
    \"facility_id\": 12345,
    \"facility_status\": \"Failed\",
    \"ownership_status\": \"Success\",
    \"level_status\": \"Success\",
    \"level_option_status\": \"Failed\",
    \"request_type\": \"Create\",
    \"dhis_uid\": \"abcd1234efg\"
}"

const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost/admin/hfr-dhis-exchange/resend"
);

const headers = {
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json",
};

let body = {
    "log_id": 456,
    "facility_id": 12345,
    "facility_status": "Failed",
    "ownership_status": "Success",
    "level_status": "Success",
    "level_option_status": "Failed",
    "request_type": "Create",
    "dhis_uid": "abcd1234efg"
};

fetch(url, {
    method: "POST",
    headers,
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
}).then(response => response.json());

Filter Facility Status Details Report

requires authentication

Filters facility status details by state, LGA, and status. Status codes are mapped to multiple related status IDs:

  • Status 2 → [2, 9, 16] (Requested states)
  • Status 3 → [3, 10, 17] (Verified states)
  • Status 4 → [4, 11, 18] (Validated states)
  • Status 5 → [5, 12, 19] (Published/Updated states)
  • Status 7 → [7, 14, 21] (Rejected states)
  • Other status codes are used directly

Administration - Laboratory

Endpoints for listing, creating, updating, viewing, and searching laboratory facilities.

Note:

  • Most methods return Blade views for the web UI.
  • Some endpoints return an HTML partial (e.g., show()).
  • API consumers should treat the responses as HTML unless explicitly JSON.

Search Laboratories

Performs an advanced search using multiple filters:

  • State, LGA, Ward
  • Facility name
  • Level of care
  • Ownership
  • Operational status
  • Registration & license status
  • Geo-code completeness

Returns paginated filtered results.

Example request:
curl --request GET \
    --get "http://localhost/admin/laboratory/search?state_id=25&lga_id=7&ward_id=0&facility_name=%22General+Hospital%22&geo_codes=16" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json"
const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost/admin/laboratory/search"
);

const params = {
    "state_id": "25",
    "lga_id": "7",
    "ward_id": "0",
    "facility_name": ""General Hospital"",
    "geo_codes": "16",
};
Object.keys(params)
    .forEach(key => url.searchParams.append(key, params[key]));

const headers = {
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json",
};

fetch(url, {
    method: "GET",
    headers,
}).then(response => response.json());

    --form "resourcefile=@C:\Users\mails\AppData\Local\Temp\phpF001.tmp"

);

    "Content-Type": "multipart/form-data",
    "Accept": "application/json",
};

body.append('filename', 'architecto');
body.append('resourcefile', document.querySelector('input[name="resourcefile"]').files[0]);

Administration Pharmacy

Endpoints for listing, creating, updating, viewing, and searching pharmacy facilities.

Note:

  • Most endpoints return Blade views for the Web UI.
  • Some endpoints (e.g., show()) return HTML partials.
  • JSON is returned only for error responses.

Search Pharmacies

Performs an advanced search with multiple filters:

  • State, LGA, Ward
  • Facility name
  • Geo-code completeness
  • Ownership
  • Operational status
  • Registration status
  • License status

Returns paginated results in UI view.

Example request:
curl --request GET \
    --get "http://localhost/admin/pharmacies/search?state_id=25&lga_id=108&ward_id=0&facility_name=%22Pharm+Care%22&geo_codes=16&ownership_id=2&operational_status_id=1" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json"
const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost/admin/pharmacies/search"
);

const params = {
    "state_id": "25",
    "lga_id": "108",
    "ward_id": "0",
    "facility_name": ""Pharm Care"",

Authentication

Token-based Login Flow

These endpoints handle the second step of a two-factor login flow. After submitting username/password, the system sends a token to the user and stores temporary login details in the session. The user must validate the token here before being logged in.

Display the token verification page.

This endpoint shows the token entry screen to the user, but only if a token has been generated and stored in the session during the login flow.

If no token exists in the current session, the user is redirected to /.

    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json"

);

Response

Response Fields

Verify the submitted token and complete login.

Validates the token submitted by the user against the token stored in the session. If the token has expired, or does not match, the user is redirected back with an error.

Upon successful validation, the system logs the user in using the stored user ID and clears the token session data, then redirects to /administrator.

Facility Approval Tracking

This controller manages the tracking and filtering of facility approval requests. It provides endpoints for viewing pending, validated, and published facility changes.

These endpoints are primarily used by administrators and state-level officers to monitor the approval workflow of health facility data.

Facility Approval Tracking - Facility Validation

This controller handles all validation-related workflows for health facility approval. It allows authorized users to view pending validations, approve or reject facility requests, recall validations, and track validation actions.

All actions are logged and tied to user permissions (State and LGA level).

Display all pending facility validation requests.

Shows all facilities that require validation, filtered based on user permissions.

  • State-level users can see all requests in the state.
  • LGA-level users can only see requests for their assigned LGAs.

Facility Approval Tracking - Record Updates

Endpoints that provide detailed audit comparison between the current and updated records of a health facility. This helps reviewers and approvers understand what changed in each facility record during the verification, validation, or publication stages.

View differences between old and updated facility records.

This endpoint retrieves the detailed audit trail and compares old versus new values for a given facility update request.

It shows changes to metadata such as ownership, location, level of care, and service availability. The view also displays the corresponding audit data and allows reviewers to approve or reject updates at different workflow stages.

Example request:
curl --request GET \
    --get "http://localhost/admin/hospitals/approvals/updated/16/16" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json"
const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost/admin/hospitals/approvals/updated/16/16"
);

const headers = {
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json",
};

fetch(url, {
    method: "GET",
    headers,
}).then(response => response.json());

Example response (200, success):


View showing old and new facility data side by side.

Example response (404, not_found):


Facility record or audit not found.

Get Facility Updates Report

Retrieves facilities that were created or updated within predefined time periods. Useful for tracking recent changes to the facility registry. This endpoint is publicly accessible without authentication.

Example request:
curl --request GET \
    --get "http://localhost/facilities/latest-updates/view?report=1" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json"
const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost/facilities/latest-updates/view"
);

const params = {
    "report": "1",
};
Object.keys(params)
    .forEach(key => url.searchParams.append(key, params[key]));

const headers = {
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json",
};

fetch(url, {
    method: "GET",
    headers,
}).then(response => response.json());

Get Filtered Statistics

Retrieves facility statistics filtered by state and facility type. Returns different data structures based on facility type:

  • Hospitals & Laboratories: Include level and ownership breakdowns
  • Pharmacies & Imaging Centers: Include ownership breakdowns only

When state_id = 0 (all states), data is aggregated by state. When specific state is selected, data is broken down by LGA within that state. This endpoint is publicly accessible without authentication.

Example request:
curl --request GET \
    --get "http://localhost/statistics/tables/filter" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json" \
    --data "{
    \"state_id\": 1,
    \"facility_type_id\": 1
}"

const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost/statistics/tables/filter"
);

const headers = {
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json",
};

let body = {
    "state_id": 1,
    "facility_type_id": 1
};

fetch(url, {
    method: "GET",
    headers,
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
}).then(response => response.json());

Statistics - Charts & Visualizations

APIs for accessing chart-ready data and visualizations of healthcare facility statistics. Provides data formatted for chart libraries (pie charts, bar charts, etc.) including facility distributions by ownership, level, and geographic location. Also includes population-to-facility ratio analysis. Data is cached for performance. No authentication required.

Display National Charts Dashboard

Returns chart-ready data for visualizing national hospital statistics including:

  • Distribution by facility level (pie/bar chart data)
  • Distribution by ownership type (pie/bar chart data)
  • Breakdown by state (table/bar chart data)

Data is formatted with 'name' and 'y' fields for direct use in charting libraries like Highcharts. Results are cached for 30-60 minutes for optimal performance. This endpoint is publicly accessible without authentication.

Example request:
curl --request GET \
    --get "http://localhost/statistics/charts" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json"
const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost/statistics/charts"
);

const headers = {
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json",
};

fetch(url, {
    method: "GET",
    headers,
}).then(response => response.json());

Get Filtered Chart Data

Returns chart-ready data filtered by facility type and state. Response structure varies by facility type:

  • Hospitals & Laboratories: Include level and ownership charts (view: statistic_charts)
  • Pharmacies & Imaging Centers: Include ownership chart only (view: statistic_charts2)

When state_id = 0, shows national aggregation. When specific state selected, shows state-specific data with LGA breakdown. This endpoint is publicly accessible without authentication.

Example request:
curl --request POST \
    "http://localhost/statistics/charts/filter" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json" \
    --data "{
    \"state_id\": 1,
    \"facility_type_id\": 1
}"

const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost/statistics/charts/filter"
);

const headers = {
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json",
};

let body = {
    "state_id": 1,
    "facility_type_id": 1
};

fetch(url, {
    method: "POST",
    headers,
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
}).then(response => response.json());

Display Population Index Dashboard

Shows the population-to-facility ratio (people per facility) at national level, aggregated by state. Lower numbers indicate better facility coverage. Calculation: State Population ÷ Number of Hospitals in State = People per Facility

Data is formatted as separate arrays for states and their corresponding ratios, ready for bar chart visualization. Cached for 60 minutes. This endpoint is publicly accessible without authentication.

Example request:
curl --request GET \
    --get "http://localhost/statistics/populationindex" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json"
const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost/statistics/populationindex"
);

const headers = {
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json",
};

fetch(url, {
    method: "GET",
    headers,
}).then(response => response.json());

Request   

GET statistics/populationindex

Headers

Content-Type        

Example: application/json

Accept        

Example: application/json

Get Filtered Population Index

Returns population-to-facility ratio filtered by state.

  • When state_id = 0: Shows ratio by state (national view)
  • When specific state selected: Shows ratio by LGA within that state

The ratio indicates healthcare facility coverage - lower numbers mean better facility coverage per capita. For example, 10,000 means one facility serves 10,000 people on average. This endpoint is publicly accessible without authentication.

Example request:
curl --request POST \
    "http://localhost/statistics/populationindex/filter" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json" \
    --data "{
    \"state_id\": 1
}"

const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost/statistics/populationindex/filter"
);

const headers = {
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json",
};

let body = {
    "state_id": 1
};

fetch(url, {
    method: "POST",
    headers,
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
}).then(response => response.json());
